identity.real_world_identity_notes: FIA evidence establishes the S7 competition identity, and specialist technical reporting supports a six-speed sequential transmission in the S7-R family. The record represents the distinct 2005 second-series GT1 evolution; early H-pattern technique and restored early-car cockpit equipment are not inherited as exact 2005 facts.

wheel_rim.notes: Early and restored S7-R cockpit photographs do not establish the original wheel fitted to the distinct 2005 second-series representation. Exact shape, display, shift-light and open-top details remain unknown.

notes: The 2005 second-series chassis is a distinct Oreca-revised evolution. No reviewed exact-2005 source establishes its downshift clutch, blip procedure or original wheel geometry.

RaceRoom officially lists Saleen S7R in its GTR 1 class. Saleen's own racing history identifies the S7R as its race version and dates its inaugural competition season to 2001; specialist technical reporting identifies a six-speed sequential S7-R revision introduced in 2002, while a period MotorTrend drive documents an early S7R with a six-speed straight-cut race transmission and short-throw shifter. DailySportscar records the family transition from early H-pattern to later sequential gearboxes. The checked-out repository already contains the compatible curated record saleen-s7-r-gt1, so this observation should join that record rather than create a duplicate.

claims.basis: A first-person drive and Johnny Mowlem's retrospective establish clutch and heel-and-toe technique for early H-pattern S7-Rs. Artcurial identifies the represented 2005 car as a distinct second-series evolution, and no reviewed exact-2005 source establishes its downshift clutch, manual-blip or automatic-blip procedure.
Official release, homologation context, and exact live CarModel/class observation establish the simulated identity.
Specialist family-level evidence and direct exercise of the modeled six-speed sequential stick agree; the historical source is from a later S7-R.

Direct current-game testing establishes the modeled start clutch and upshift behavior. Downshift and cockpit observations are preserved separately as simulator overrides and do not define the real 2005 car.

A restored early S7-R cockpit shows a near-circular rim, but it does not establish the original equipment of the distinct 2005 second-series representation. No reviewed exact-2005 source establishes wheel shape, display, shift lights or open-top geometry.

RSS identifies the exact Shadow implementation, and its installed metadata, American V8 layout, body, specifications, and bundled Saleen and period FIA GT liveries converge on the existing Saleen S7-R GT1 record. The in-game year 2000 is not promoted as a real-car revision because no readable package field declares it and the skins span later seasons.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
